ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, $CD$ bisects $\angle ACB$, through point B draw $BD\perp CD$ with the foot of the perpendicular at point D, connect AD. If $AB=3$ and $BC=4$, what is the area of $\triangle ABD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, extend $BD$ to intersect $AC$ at point $E$. In the right triangle $\triangle ABC$, $AB=3$, $BC=4$,\\
$\therefore AC=\sqrt{AB^{2}+BC^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}=5$,\\
$\because CD$ bisects $\angle ACB$, and $BD\perp CD$,\\
$\therefore BC=CE=4$, $AE=AC-CE=1$, $BD=ED$,\\
$\therefore \frac{S_{\triangle ABE}}{S_{\triangle ABC}}=\frac{AE}{AC}=\frac{1}{5}$,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle ABE}=\frac{1}{5}S_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{5}\times\frac{1}{2}\times3\times4=\frac{6}{5}$,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle ABD}=\frac{1}{2}S_{\triangle ABE}=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{6}{5}=\boxed{\frac{3}{5}}$.

From the text take AB=3, BC=4, ∠B=90°, and CD is the internal angle bisector at C. Set coordinates B=(0,0), A=(0,3), C=(4,0), matching the visual right-triangle orientation. The unit direction from C to B is (-1,0), and the unit direction from C to A is (-4/5,3/5), so the internal angle-bisector direction is their sum, proportional to (-3,1). Hence CD has slope -1/3 through C. Since BD is perpendicular to CD and passes through B, BD has slope 3, so its equation is y=3x. Intersect y=3x with CD, for example y=(4-x)/3, to get D=(2/5,6/5). The area of triangle ABD is then one half times base AB=3 times the horizontal distance from D to line AB, namely 2/5, giving 3/5.

按图中方向建立坐标系：令 B=(0,0)，A=(0,3)，C=(4,0)，这与 AB=3、BC=4、∠ABC=90° 相符。由 C 指向 B 的单位方向向量为 (-1,0)，由 C 指向 A 的单位方向向量为 (-4/5,3/5)。因为 CD 是 ∠ACB 的内部角平分线，所以其方向向量与二者和向量成比例：(-1,0)+(-4/5,3/5)=(-9/5,3/5)，即方向可取为 (-3,1)。因此 CD 的斜率为 -1/3，且过 C=(4,0)，方程为 y=(4-x)/3。又因为 BD⊥CD，BD 过 B=(0,0)，所以 BD 的斜率为 3，方程为 y=3x。联立 y=3x 与 y=(4-x)/3，得 3x=(4-x)/3，即 9x=4-x，10x=4，所以 x=2/5，y=6/5，故 D=(2/5,6/5)。三角形 ABD 以 AB 为底，AB=3；D 到直线 AB，即 x=0 的水平距离为 2/5。因此 S_{△ABD}=1/2×3×2/5=3/5。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, $CD$ bisects $\angle ACB$, through point B draw $BD\perp CD$ with the foot of the perpendicular at point D, connect $AD$. If $AB=3$ and $BC=4$, what is the area of $\triangle ABD$?
raw_record.answer:
As shown in the figure, extend $BD$ to intersect $AC$ at point $E$. In the right triangle $\triangle ABC$, $AB=3$, $BC=4$, 
$\therefore AC=\sqrt{AB^{2}+BC^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}=5$, 
$\because CD$ bisects $\angle ACB$, and $BD\perp CD$, 
$\therefore BC=CE=4$, $AE=AC-CE=1$, $BD=ED$, 
$\therefore \frac{S_{\triangle ABE}}{S_{\triangle ABC}}=\frac{AE}{AC}=\frac{1}{5}$, 
$\therefore S_{\triangle ABE}=\frac{1}{5}S_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{5}\times\frac{1}{2}\times3\times4=\frac{6}{5}$, 
$\therefore S_{\triangle ABD}=\frac{1}{2}S_{\triangle ABE}=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{6}{5}=\boxed{\frac{3}{5}}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there is a triangle ABC, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is on the right, AB is vertical, BC is horizontal, and ∠ABC is shown as a right angle. In the figure, line segment CD is drawn from C toward the interior of the triangle, D is located inside near the left; there is line segment BD from B to D, and there is a right-angle mark at D, indicating BD ⟂ CD; AD is also connected.
Reasoning: Given AB=3, BC=4, and ∠ABC=90°, so AC=sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5. According to the method, extend BD to intersect AC at E. Because CD bisects ∠ACB, and E is on AC, CD is also the angle bisector of ∠BCE; also because BD ⟂ CD, and B, D, E are collinear, so CD ⟂ BE. In triangle BCE, the angle bisector CD drawn from C is also perpendicular to BE, therefore triangle BCE is an isosceles triangle, BC=CE, and D is the midpoint of BE. Thus CE=4, AE=AC−CE=5−4=1. Triangle ABE and triangle ABC take the line on which AC lies as the same base-line direction, and the height from B to AC is the same, so the area ratio S(ABE):S(ABC)=AE:AC=1:5. Also S(ABC)=1/2×3×4=6, therefore S(ABE)=6/5. Because D is the midpoint of BE, AD divides triangle ABE into two triangles of equal area, so S(ABD)=1/2×6/5=3/5.
